name: Irregular (shādhdh)
definition: A usage or form that departs from the rule (the qiyās) or from what most Arabs say; kept where it was heard but not taken as a model.
body: The commentaries grade usage: muṭṭarid (regular, following the rule), kathīr (frequent), qalīl (rare), nādir (very rare) and shādhdh (going against the rule). Ibn Jinnī distinguished four cases: regular in rule and usage (the doer in rafʿ), regular in rule but rare in usage, rare in rule but regular in usage, and irregular in both.

A form can be shādhdh by the rule and still perfectly good Arabic: the commentators' example is istaḥwadha in the Qurʾān, which keeps its wāw where the rule of iʿlāl would turn it to alif. Such a form is kept where it was heard and not used to build others. A shādhdh reading of the Qurʾān is a different thing: one outside the canonical readings.

examples.text: Q 58:19: istaḥwadha keeps its wāw against the rule of iʿlāl; irregular by analogy, eloquent in use.
